_schema_comment: Each entry has the following fields:

_fields.type: One of: litigation | gao | ig | other. Required.
_fields.title: Short human-readable title of the finding or case. Required.
_fields.url: Canonical URL (court docket, GAO report, IG report). Required.
_fields.confirmed: true = manually verified match; false = lead only. Required.
_fields.added_by: Initials or name of curator who added this entry. Required.

_how_to_add: 1. Run gsa_gc_search_litigation to find candidate CourtListener cases.
2. Manually verify the case relates to the specific use case (name matches are often false positives).
3. Add a new JSON object below with confirmed: true only after verification.
4. Re-run scripts/build_index.py if risk scores need updating.
5. Never auto-populate this file from search results.

title: National Organization of Veterans' Advocates, Inc. v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs — Fed. Cir. 25-1399
summary: NOVA petitioned the Federal Circuit under 38 U.S.C. § 502 to challenge a VA regulatory action; case voluntarily dismissed June 2025 before merits briefing — specific rule at issue not confirmed.
added_by: Gem Cortez via CourtListener MCP search
notes: Lead only — voluntarily dismissed 2025-06-17 by joint stipulation before any merits brief was filed. The petition originated directly from the VA, and NOVA (the largest VSO litigator) was petitioner, making this structurally relevant to VBA automated benefits processes. Cannot confirm AI link without reading the underlying petition. Docket entries are available on PACER: gov.uscourts.cafc.22671. Needs manual follow-up to identify the specific VA rule challenged.

title: Anthropic PBC v. U.S. Dept. of War — APA AI challenge, VA named defendant (N.D. Cal. 3:26-cv-01996; D.C. Cir. 26-1049)
summary: D.C. Circuit upheld exclusion of Anthropic's Claude from federal agency supply chains under FASCSА; VA was named as a party defendant but the case concerned DoD/supply chain security, not VA benefits AI.
added_by: Gem Cortez via CourtListener MCP search
notes: Lead only — NOT directly about VA benefits AI. D.C. Cir. opinion (26-1049, decided 2026-09-25) held the Department of War's exclusion of Claude from its supply chain was lawful under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act of 2018. VA was a named federal defendant but not the subject of the AI exclusion. Included here as a structural precedent: the APA and FASCSА framework used in this case could be applied to challenge opaque GenAI tools (like M-CAT) in federal benefits adjudication. Do not count as confirmed litigation against M-CAT.

title: Structural risk: PACT Act benefits litigation ecosystem — no docket specifically naming co-pay AI
summary: Active Federal Circuit litigation ecosystem challenging VA benefit access decisions under the PACT Act; AI-driven co-pay exemption errors would flow directly into this well-litigated domain.
added_by: Gem Cortez via CourtListener MCP search
notes: No docket specifically names the PACT Act Co-Pay Exemption Prediction Tool. Reference docket is Transgender American Veterans Assoc. v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs (Fed. Cir. 24-1714, filed 2024-04-19, decided 2025-01-14) — a 22-state/VSO coalition case against the VA Secretary, demonstrating the active, organized Federal Circuit litigation environment around VA benefit access. Any AI-driven wrongful co-pay exemption denial under the PACT Act would be litigable in this same venue.
